title: Exact continuous realizations and restriction triangles
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, a finite intermediate field $E$, and $F\in\{E,\Omega\}$. Let $\Pi$ be a profinite group (compact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected), and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space with a jointly continuous $E$-linear $\Pi$-action [def-pod-l-adic-representations]. Let $U\subseteq V$ be a $\Pi$-stable $E$-subspace, and put $Q=V/U$ with the induced action and usual finite-dimensional topology. Put $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring] and $W_F(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E W)$ for $W=U,V,Q$, with finite-dimensional product norm topologies. Use the induced condensed actions in internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module] and their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The canonical sequence
$$0\longrightarrow U_F\longrightarrow V_F\longrightarrow Q_F\longrightarrow0$$
is short exact in $\mathcal A_{C_F}(\Pi)$ and split exact after forgetting the action, by a splitting natural in the profinite parameter $S$. It gives the distinguished triangle $U_F[0]\to V_F[0]\to Q_F[0]\to U_F[1]$ [def-weil-triangulated-category, def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift]. For every topological group $H$ and continuous homomorphism $u:H\to\Pi$, the canonical derived restriction transformation $b_u$ of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] gives a morphism of the $R\Gamma_\Pi$ and $R\Gamma_H\operatorname{Res}_u$ images of this triangle, with components $b_u(U_F)$, $b_u(V_F)$, $b_u(Q_F)$, including the square on the connecting arrow. The splitting need not be equivariant; no completeness of $\Omega$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $i:U\to V$ and $q:V\to Q$. By [lem-sfb-continuous-representation-subquotients], $U,Q$ have their usual finite-dimensional topologies, their induced actions are jointly continuous, and $i,q$ are continuous equivariant linear maps. Choose an $E$-basis $(e_j)$ of $Q$ and lifts $v_j\in V$. Its coordinate map is a homeomorphism, by the usual finite-dimensional topology in the hypotheses. Apply [lem-sfb-topological-basis-lift-section] with $A=E$, $M=V$, $N=Q$: $s(\sum_j a_je_j)=\sum_j a_jv_j$ is a continuous linear section of $q$. Define $r(v)\in U$ by $i(r(v))=v-s(q(v))$. This lies in $U$ because its image under $q$ is zero, and is continuous into the subspace topology because the displayed $V$-valued map is continuous. Direct substitution gives $ri=1$, $rs=0$, $qi=0$, $qs=1$ and $ir+sq=1$. No equivariance is claimed for $s$ or $r$.

proof.text: Choose a basis $(u_a)$ of $U$. Then $(i(u_a),v_j)$ is a basis of $V$: applying $q$ to a linear relation kills all coefficients of the $v_j$, and subtracting $s(q(v))$ expresses every remaining vector in $U$. For any of these bases $(w_k)$ of $W=U,V,Q$, identify $F\otimes_E W$ with $F^{\{k\}}$ by $f\otimes\sum_k a_kw_k\mapsto(fa_k)_k$, with inverse $(c_k)\mapsto\sum_k c_k\otimes w_k$. The first formula is balanced, and the two composites are identities by distributivity. These are precisely the product norm coordinates stipulated in the statement. The tensor extensions $i_F,q_F,s_F,r_F$ have finite matrices with entries in $E\subset F$, hence are continuous: each output coordinate is a finite sum of constant multiples of input coordinates. The five identities of step 1 hold after tensor extension. For $W=U,V,Q$, the matrix entries $a_{kl}(g)$ of the action are continuous $E$-valued functions of $g$, obtained by acting on $w_l$ and taking coordinates. Their images in $F$ are continuous because the extended norm restricts to the norm on $E$. Thus $(g,(x_l))\mapsto(\sum_l a_{kl}(g)x_l)_k$ is jointly continuous over $F$. The group laws and equivariance of $i_F,q_F$ follow on pure tensors, hence on their finite sums. Only finite sums and products occur; no completeness of $F$ is used.

proof.text: Use [def-sfb-continuous-representation-condensation] for the jointly continuous actions of step 2. It gives the internal action modules $U_F,V_F,Q_F$ and the equivariant morphisms induced by $i_F,q_F$. For the trivial group the same realization statement gives underlying internal-module morphisms induced by $s_F,r_F$; restriction to the trivial group leaves the section realization unchanged. On every profinite $S$, their formulas are postcomposition. In particular $q_{F,*}s_{F,*}=1$, $r_{F,*}i_{F,*}=1$, $r_{F,*}s_{F,*}=0$, and $i_{F,*}r_{F,*}+s_{F,*}q_{F,*}=1$. These identities exhibit the underlying module $V_F$ as the direct sum of $U_F$ and $Q_F$, with the given inclusion and projection. All maps commute with precomposition $S'\to S$, since $(s_F\circ f)\circ t=s_F\circ(f\circ t)$, and likewise for $r_F,i_F,q_F$. Therefore this is a split short exact sequence of internal modules, with splitting natural in $S$. The forgetful functor detects exactness by [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], so the equivariant sequence is short exact as well. This uses a splitting only after forgetting the action.

proof.text: The action category is abelian by [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Regard the short exact sequence of step 3 as a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes concentrated in degree zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to obtain its canonical distinguished triangle $T=(U_F[0]\to V_F[0]\to Q_F[0]\xrightarrow{\delta}U_F[1])$. By the restriction calculus, $R\Gamma_\Pi$ and $R\Gamma_H D(\operatorname{Res}_u)$ are triangulated, so their images of $T$ are distinguished triangles with the canonical shift comparisons. The exactness needed here concerns the action and derived categories; it does not assert that taking invariants is exact.

proof.text: Put $A=R\Gamma_\Pi$ and $B=R\Gamma_H D(\operatorname{Res}_u)$. The natural transformation $b_u:A\to B$ of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] is natural in derived morphisms and commutes with the canonical shifts. Naturality at $i_F[0]$ and $q_F[0]$ gives the first two triangle squares. Naturality at the actual derived boundary $\delta:Q_F[0]\to U_F[1]$ gives $b_u(U_F[1])\circ A(\delta)=B(\delta)\circ b_u(Q_F[0])$. After the canonical shift identifications, its left component is $b_u(U_F[0])[1]$. This is exactly the connecting-arrow square. Hence the three specified components form a morphism of the image triangles. This argument applies to every topological $H$ and continuous $u$; it uses the derived restriction transformation, with no identification with underived continuous cochains.

Applied with the trivial group, this turns the pointwise split identities into morphism identities. The splitting is non-equivariant and natural in S.
